title: Trigonometric Ratios of Any Angle and Their Graphs
seo_title: Trigonometric Graphs – SSS 2 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Find sine, cosine and tangent of angles from 0° to 360°; use the signs in the four quadrants; draw and read graphs of y = sin x and y = cos x; solve simple trigonometric equations. (summary of the NERDC SSS 2 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free SSS 2 maths worksheets on trigonometry from 0° to 360°: reference angles, signs in the quadrants, exact values and graphs of sine and cosine. 100 questions with answers.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • For an angle between 90° and 360°, find the reference angle with the x-axis.
  • Use the quadrant to give the sign: sin 150° = sin 30° = 1/2, cos 150° = −cos 30°.
  • y = sin x and y = cos x repeat every 360° and stay between −1 and 1.

Examples

Example

cos 240°

Reference angle 60°, quadrant 3

Answer: −1/2

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Using the angle with the y-axisThe reference angle is with the x-axis.
Wrong signUse the quadrant rule.
Thinking sin x can be 2Sine is always between −1 and 1.

items.q: Find the exact value of cos 210°.
items.e: 210° is in quadrant 3 with reference angle 30°. cos 30° = √3/2, and the sign there is −: −√3/2.

items.q: What is the period of y = sin 4x?
items.e: The period of sin bx is 360° ÷ b = 360° ÷ 4 = 90°.

items.q: What is the amplitude of y = 3 cos x?
items.e: The amplitude is the number in front of cos: 3. The graph goes from −3 to 3.
